newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan cuts off Bahamas for readying China ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cuts off Bahamas for readying China ties.

text.p: Diplomatically isolated Taiwan on Sunday severed ties with the Bahamas, saying it had learnt the Caribbean islands were preparing to establish ties with Taiwan's arch-rival, China.
"The Republic of China government announces that it is severing ties with the Bahamas immediately," the foreign ministry said in a brief statement.
"It has also suspended all treaties and cooperations between the two countries and recalled its ambassador," the statement said.

The foreign ministry's surprise announcement cut back the number of countries that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government to 30. That number will fall to 29 later this year when Taipei's biggest diplomatic ally, South Africa, switches ties to Beijing.
It also comes at a time when Taiwan's newly- established ties with the tiny African state of Sao Tome are reported to be under threat.

"In recent years, the Bahamas has betrayed its words and yielded to communist China's temptation...it plans to develop full diplomatic ties with communist China in the near future," the statement said.
The government's repeated attempts to rescue the Bahamas ties were in vein, it said.
The Bahamas, home to about 254,000 people, is a chain of islands east of Florida. It established diplomatic relations with Taiwan in 1989.
"The move has seriously damaged the national interest of the Republic of China," it added.

Taiwan and China have been bitter political rivals since a civil war spilt them in 1949. Beijing regards Taiwan as a rebel province ineligible to international recognition and warns other countries against establishing ties with the island.

Taiwan on Saturday said it would not give up newly-established formal ties with West Africa's small twin-island nation of Sao Tome and Principe despite reports that Sao Tome's cabinet had rejected the new links.
Taiwan announced on May 6 that it had established formal ties with Sao Tome, scoring a minor victory in its four-decade diplomatic tug-of-war with China.
China said it was absolutely opposed to Sao Tome establishing diplomatic relations with Taiwan, but stopped short of saying it would sever official ties with the African republic.
Taiwan and China have competed aggressively for diplomatic recognition since 1949, often accusing each other of using large sums of cash and aid to woo potential backers.
Taiwan, which has insisted its 21 million people need to have a living space in the international community, said it would not be discouraged by China's oppression.
"Over the past years, communist China is intensifying its efforts to oppress us in international affairs," the foreign ministry said on Sunday.
"Facing such a situation...we have to maintain our firm position and continue to expand our international living space with a positive and pragmatic attitude," it added.
